Simon: Heads-up — noticed a 25% p99 latency bump on seq=128 generation on the SM92 pool after last week's driver bump. Looks like kernel routing fell back to the scalar/emu path for a lot of requests.
Maria: Ugh. Do we have a repro microbench? Any kernel selection logs?
Simon: Yes — attached minimal repro logs (pasted):
```
arch_probe: sm=92, driver=540.12, tc=1, bf16=1, fp8=0
kernel_select: chosen=matmul_fast_tc_bf16, path=fast_gemm
runtime: override -> fallback_kernel=matmul_generic_no_tc
perf: seq=128 batch=1 p50=22ms p95=74ms p99=138ms
```
But on many runs it flips to `matmul_generic_no_tc` which is ~2x slower for our shape.
Alex: Two quick thoughts: 1) the capability probe might be reporting TC availability but not validating behaviour (driver ABI change?). 2) sequence-length gating could be mis-evaluating the threshold and forcing a non-TC code-path for large seqlen because of a batching heuristic bug.
Maria: Could the KV cache prefetch/eviction be thrashing at seq128 and causing kernel to think it should avoid the tc path? We've seen prefetch heuristics bounce before.
Simon: Here's a snippet from the runtime decision log around the flip: 
```
[decision] seq=128 kv_hits=0.18 last_kv_miss_ms=9.2 kernel_pref_score=0.82
[heuristic] score_adjusted_for_kv=-0.65 -> final=0.17 -> choose fallback
```
That -0.65 looks aggressive. Not obvious where that constant came from.
Alex: That constant is from the batching/kvcache gating table (heuristics.cpp). We added it years ago to avoid tensorcore jitter on small batch/missy workloads; maybe the driver upgrade changed memory latencies and now it over-penalizes.
Maria: Action plan proposal: add a direct microprobe that runs a tiny GEMM with bf16 on-device and measures throughput (3 iterations) and asserts >X TFLOPS. Use that to validate actual TC performance rather than trusting flags. If microprobe fails, mark TC=false for that driver+SM combination and fallback to tuned generic kernels.
Simon: Agreed. Also add a short-circuit: if seq_len >= 96 and batch<=2, prefer TC path unless microprobe indicates <70% expected perf. That should avoid the regression for our seq128 p99.
Alex: I'll open a small PR with: 1) microprobe binary invoked at probe-time, 2) a new threshold config, 3) a histogram metric `runtime.probe.tc_verified_ratio`.
Maria: Please also add CI test that runs the microprobe in the container (mocked by a small golden log) so we catch API/ABI parsing regressions in future driver bumps.
CI Bot: job-runtime-probe-unit-tests queued — will run on PR. :white_check_mark:
infra-bot: Scheduling a canary rollback of the 540.x driver on 3 nodes in the SM92 pool for the next 2 hours to verify impact. Will report metrics to #eng-sre.
Simon: Thanks — I'll collect perf traces (perf_events + nvtx) from the affected instances and attach to the PR. If the microprobe shows mismatch, we gate TC at init and ship a hotfix.
Alex: One more note — add a debug flag `RUNTIME_FORCE_TC_VERIFY=1` so infra can trigger probe-only mode on a live host without full rollout.
Maria: Cool. Assigning: Alex (PR + probe binary), Simon (traces + repro), Maria (config + CI test). Target: hotfix branch by EOD tomorrow. :clock10:
Simon: Sounds good. I'll paste the nvprof snippet in the PR and tag you both. Thanks. :thumbsup:
